compare.title: Whether 2025 looks high or low depends on the year it is compared with
compare.subtitle: Years of median household income to pay for a constant-quality four-room resale flat, as a change from the starting year the reader picks
compare.tally: From 11 of the 12 starting years, 2025 comes out higher. From 2013 it comes out lower.

starts.headline: fewer years of income than in 2013
starts.verdict: The flat took 5.04 years of median household income in 2025, against 5.43 in 2013: 0.39 fewer.
starts.why: Between those years the price rose 40% and income rose 51%.

explain: Each point is one year: the price of the same kind of four-room resale flat, divided by what the median household earned in a year. Lower means the flat took less income.

Tap a point, drag across the chart, or use the slider and the arrow buttons. The card under the chart reads that year: the value, the change from the year before, where it ranks, and how far it sits from the first year.

The sentences in the card are worked out when the page is built, from the same data file as the line. None is typed by hand and none comes from a live model, so the card and the chart cannot disagree.
compare: Pick a starting year with the slider or the two buttons. The line then shows every year as a change from that year, in per cent. The starting year sits on the zero line.
Above the zero line the flat took more years of income than in the starting year; below it, fewer. The card gives the answer for 2025 in words.
The bars under the chart give the same answer for every starting year at once, so the reader can see how much the answer depends on where the comparison starts.
This is a reading of what happened. It says nothing about any one household, and nothing about what prices will do.

steps.text: 2013 was a price peak: the flat cost 5.43 years of median income.
2019 was the low: 4.04 years. Starting a comparison here makes everything after it look worse.
2025: 5.04 years. More than in 2019, fewer than in 2013.

howto: Each point is one year: the price of the same kind of four-room resale flat, divided by what the median household earned in a year.
Lower means the flat took less income. Drag the slider, or press Play, to move through the years.
The second panel sets both the price and the income to 100 in the first year, so the two can be compared on one scale.
source_line: Source: HDB resale transactions and SingStat household income, via the piece's own pipeline.
